text:
We extend Balmer's tensor-triangular geometry to arbitrary presentably symmetric monoidal $\infty$-categories $\mathcal V$ by introducing the atomic smashing frame. This construction is functorial in $\mathcal V$, recovers the classical Balmer spectrum in the stable compactly-rigidly generated case, and yields a formulation of the telescope conjecture for arbitrary $\mathcal V$. Using dualizable and locally rigid $\infty$-categories, we identify smashing ideals with locally rigid localizations and establish recollement results for smashing frames and atomic smashing frames. As a consequence, we obtain a recollement principle for the telescope conjecture. We also establish descent for the telescope conjecture along several natural classes of coverings. As a principal application to chromatic homotopy theory, we analyze the structure of the smashing frame of $\mathrm{Sp}$. We prove a prime decomposition in terms of the smashing frames of the $p$-local $\infty$-categories $\mathrm{Sp}_{(p)}$ and, at each prime, an embedding into the product of the smashing frames of the monochromatic layers $\mathrm{Sp}_{T(n)}$. In particular, the spatiality of the smashing frame of $\mathrm{Sp}$ reduces entirely to that of $\mathrm{Sp}_{T(n)}$. Beyond the stable setting, we characterize the telescope conjecture for $\infty$-topoi in terms of smashing fields, and for connective module categories and hypercomplete connective sheaves in terms of Pierce-type conditions. Finally, we introduce the Serre smashing frame. Over a connective $\mathbb{E}_\infty$-ring $R$, this frame sits between the atomic and usual smashing frames, providing an intermediate structural layer in the study of the telescope conjecture for the connective $R$-module $\infty$-category.

1 Introduction 1.1 Background The development of stable homotopy theory over the past few decades has been largely guided by the theory of chromatic filtration. At the core of this theoretical framework is the telescope conjecture, proposed by Ravenel in the late 1970s and formally published in 1984. The conjecture asserts that for any height n n , localization with respect to Morava K K -theory K ⁡ ( n ) K(n) is equivalent to localization with respect to the telescope of a v n v_{n} -self map on a finite type n n complex. Although Mahowald and Miller proved the correctness of the conjecture at heights n = 0 n=0 and n = 1 n=1 , respectively in [ 42 ] and [ 45 ] , its validity at higher heights remained an open question for decades. Recently, Burklund, Hahn, Levy, and Schlank [ 20 ] resolved this question by conducting a deep analysis of the algebraic K K -theory of chromatic filtration, explicitly falsifying the telescope conjecture at heights n ≥ 2 n\geq 2 . The failure of the classical telescope conjecture for the ∞ \infty -category Sp \mathrm{Sp} of spectra motivates the development of a broader categorical framework to precisely quantify this telescopic gap. Beyond its chromatic origins, the telescope conjecture has evolved into a fundamental problem in the study of tensor-triangular geometry ( t ​ t tt -geometry). Abstracted from the foundational works of Bousfield and Ravenel [ 18 , 51 ] , generalizations of the telescope conjecture have been naturally explored within compactly-rigidly generated t ​ t tt -categories, asking whether every smashing ideal is compactly generated. While it fails for Sp \mathrm{Sp} , the telescope conjecture has been shown to hold in several algebraic contexts. Most notably, Neeman [ 46 ] established it for derived categories of commutative Noetherian rings, a result later generalized by Antieau and Stevenson [ 2 ] to representations of quivers over commutative Noetherian rings, fully proving the conjecture for Dynkin quivers. A key property of a compactly-rigidly generated t ​ t tt -category 𝒞 \mathcal{C} is that every compactly generated localizing ideal is a smashing ideal. This allows the classical Balmer frame [ 12 ] , defined as the poset of radical thick ideals of 𝒞 ω \mathcal{C}^{\omega} , to embed naturally into the smashing frame introduced in [ 11 ] : Idem f ​ ( 𝒞 ) ↪ Idem ⁡ ( 𝒞 ) . \mathrm{Idem}_{f}(\mathcal{C})\hookrightarrow\mathrm{Idem}(\mathcal{C}). In this setting, the telescope conjecture is equivalent to asking whether this canonical inclusion is an equivalence. This elegant formulation also appears in the context of higher Zariski geometry (see [ 3 , 36 ] ). However, this characterization relies heavily on the assumption of compact-rigidity. This prompts a natural structural question: Question 1.1 . Is it possible to formulate the telescope conjecture for an arbitrary big t ​ t tt -category, or more generally, for any presentably symmetric monoidal ∞ \infty -category 𝒱 ∈ CAlg ⁡ ( 𝒫 ​ r L ) \mathcal{V}\in\mathrm{CAlg}(\mathcal{P}\mathrm{r}^{L}) ? Extending the conjecture in this way fundamentally reduces to identifying a “generalized Balmer frame” for an arbitrary 𝒱 ∈ CAlg ⁡ ( 𝒫 ​ r L ) \mathcal{V}\in\mathrm{CAlg}(\mathcal{P}\mathrm{r}^{L}) . Specifically, we seek a conceptual construction that satisfies the following natural conditions: Question 1.2 . Does there exist a natural extension of the Balmer frame to an arbitrary 𝒱 ∈ CAlg ⁡ ( 𝒫 ​ r L ) \mathcal{V}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{P}\mathrm{r}^{L}) such that: (1) it depends functorially on 𝒱 \mathcal{V} , inducing a functor CAlg ⁡ ( 𝒫 ​ r L ) → 𝖥𝗋𝗆 \operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{P}\mathrm{r}^{L})\to\mathsf{Frm} ; (2) it admits a natural embedding into the smashing frame of 𝒱 \mathcal{V} ; (3) it recovers the classical Balmer frame when 𝒱 \mathcal{V} is stable and compactly-rigidly generated? The classical Balmer frame is constructed specifically from compact objects. In the classical compactly-rigidly generated setting, the notions of “absolute compactness” and “relative compactness” coincide. However, once the assumption of compact-rigidity is dropped, these two distinct categorical notions generally diverge. To establish a universal framework, it is necessary to base our constructions on “relative compactness”. Categorically, this corresponds to 𝒱 \mathcal{V} -atomic objects, which in turn yield 𝒱 \mathcal{V} -atomically generated smashing ideals. This conceptual shift will introduce the main object of study in this paper: the atomic smashing frame cIdem f ​ ( 𝒱 ) \mathrm{cIdem}_{f}(\mathcal{V}) , which provides a positive answer to Question 1.2 . 1.2 Main results Atomic Smashing Frames To formalize the generalized Balmer frame beyond the compactly-rigidly generated stable setting, particularly in potentially unstable contexts, we must identify an appropriate categorical substitute for the smashing frame. A key insight in this direction, due to Aoki, is that the correct formulation of the smashing frame relies on the poset of coidempotent objects rather than idempotent objects, though these two notions coincide in the stable setting. Definition 1.3 . Let 𝒱 ∈ CAlg ⁡ ( 𝒫 ​ r L ) \mathcal{V}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{P}\mathrm{r}^{L}) . The smashing frame of 𝒱 \mathcal{V} is defined to be the poset cIdem ⁡ ( 𝒱 ) \mathrm{cIdem}(\mathcal{V}) of coidempotent objects. The primary reason for this distinction is that the poset of idempotent objects Idem ⁡ ( 𝒱 ) \mathrm{Idem}(\mathcal{V}) fails to form a frame in general. In joint work of the author [ 36 ] , we relate smashing ideals to the theory of dualizable 𝒱 \mathcal{V} -modules. Specifically, we establish an equivalence between the smashing frame of 𝒱 \mathcal{V} and that of the ∞ \infty -category of dualizable 𝒱 \mathcal{V} -modules: cIdem ⁡ ( 𝒱 ) → ∼ x ↦ ⟨ x ⟩ cIdem ⁡ ( 𝒫 ​ r 𝒱 dbl ) . \mathrm{cIdem}(\mathcal{V})\xrightarrow[\sim]{x\mapsto\langle x\rangle}\mathrm{cIdem}(\mathcal{P}\mathrm{r}_{\mathcal{V}}^{\mathrm{dbl}}). This perspective indicates that smashing ideals can be encoded by coidempotent objects within the ∞ \infty -category of dualizable modules. Guided by this correspondence, the atomic smashing frame naturally emerges, as follows: Proposition 1.4 ( Proposition 4.1 ) . Let 𝒱 ∈ CAlg ⁡ ( 𝒫 ​ r L ) \mathcal{V}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{P}\mathrm{r}^{L}) . The image of the canonical embedding cIdem ⁡ ( 𝒫 ​ r 𝒱 at ) ↪ cIdem ⁡ ( 𝒫 ​ r 𝒱 dbl ) \mathrm{cIdem}(\mathcal{P}\mathrm{r}_{\mathcal{V}}^{\mathrm{at}})\hookrightarrow\mathrm{cIdem}(\mathcal{P}\mathrm{r}_{\mathcal{V}}^{\mathrm{dbl}}) can be identified with the 𝒱 \mathcal{V} -atomically generated smashing ideals of 𝒱 \mathcal{V} . In particular, the subposet of atomically generated smashing ideals forms a subframe. Definition 1.5 . Let 𝒱 ∈ CAlg ⁡ ( 𝒫 ​ r L ) \mathcal{V}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{P}\mathrm{r}^{L}) . A smashing ideal ℐ ↪ 𝒱 \mathcal{I}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{V} is called an atomic smashing ideal if it is generated, as a 𝒱 \mathcal{V} -submodule, by 𝒱 \mathcal{V} -atomic objects (equivalently, by dualizable objects). We define the atomic smashing frame of 𝒱 \mathcal{V} to be the subposet cIdem f ​ ( 𝒱 ) ⊂ cIdem ⁡ ( 𝒱 ) \mathrm{cIdem}_{f}(\mathcal{V})\subset\mathrm{cIdem}(\mathcal{V}) consisting of those coidempotent objects x → 𝟏 x\to\mathbf{1} whose associated smashing ideal ⟨ x ⟩ ↪ 𝒱 \langle x\rangle\hookrightarrow\mathcal{V} is atomic. This follows from the following more general statement. Proposition 1.6 ( Corollary 4.20 ) . Let 𝒱 ∈ CAlg ⁡ ( 𝒫 ​ r L ) \mathcal{V}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{P}\mathrm{r}^{L}) , and let 𝒲 ∈ CAlg ⁡ ( 𝒫 ​ r 𝒱 L ) \mathcal{W}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{P}\mathrm{r}^{L}_{\mathcal{V}}) be a locally rigid algebra over 𝒱 \mathcal{V} such that 𝒲 \mathcal{W} is 𝒱 \mathcal{V} -atomically generated. A smashing ideal ℐ ↪ 𝒲 \mathcal{I}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{W} is an atomic smashing ideal of 𝒲 \mathcal{W} if and only if it is 𝒱 \mathcal{V} -atomically generated when regarded as a 𝒱 \mathcal{V} -module. Example 1.7 . (1) Suppose that 𝒞 ∈ CAlg ⁡ ( 𝒫 ​ r st L ) \mathcal{C}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{P}\mathrm{r}_{\mathrm{st}}^{L}) is compactly generated and locally rigid over Sp \mathrm{Sp} (e.g., Sp \mathrm{Sp} , L n f ​ Sp L_{n}^{f}\mathrm{Sp} , L n ​ Sp L_{n}\mathrm{Sp} , Sp T ⁡ ( n ) \mathrm{Sp}_{T(n)} , Sp K ⁡ ( n ) \mathrm{Sp}_{K(n)} , and Sp p ​ - ​ cpl \mathrm{Sp}_{p\text{-}\mathrm{cpl}} ). Then a smashing ideal ℐ ↪ 𝒞 \mathcal{I}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{C} is atomic if and only if it is compactly generated. (2) Suppose that 𝒞 ∈ CAlg ⁡ ( 𝒫 ​ r ad L ) \mathcal{C}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{P}\mathrm{r}_{\mathrm{ad}}^{L}) is compact projectively generated and locally rigid over Sp ≥ 0 \operatorname{Sp}_{\geq 0} (e.g., Sp ≥ 0 \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq 0} , Sp G , ≥ 0 \mathrm{Sp}_{G,\geq 0} , Fil ​ ( Sp ) h ≥ 0 \mathrm{Fil}(\mathrm{Sp})_{h\geq 0} , Syn R , ≥ 0 \mathrm{Syn}_{R,\geq 0} , and DM ​ ( k , 𝐙 ⁡ [ 1 / p ] ) c ≥ 0 \mathrm{DM}(k,\mathbf{Z}[1/p])_{c\geq 0} ; see Example 7.4 for definitions). Then a smashing ideal ℐ ↪ 𝒞 \mathcal{I}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{C} is atomic if and only if it is compact projectively generated. We then establish a general coherence theorem for atomic smashing frames. This is analogous to the coherence of the classical Balmer frame. Theorem A ( Theorem 4.26 , 4.32 ) . Let 𝒱 ∈ CAlg ⁡ ( 𝒫 ​ r L ) \mathcal{V}\in\operatorname{CAlg}(\mathcal{P}\mathrm{r}^{L}) . (1) If the unit of 𝒱 \mathcal{V} is compact, then cIdem f ​ ( 𝒱 ) \mathrm{cIdem}_{f}(\mathcal{V}) is a coherent frame. (2) If the compact dualizable objects of 𝒱 \mathcal{V} generate 𝒱 \mathcal{V} as a localizing ideal, then cIdem f ​ ( 𝒱 ) \mathrm{cIdem}_{f}(\mathcal{V}) is a locally coherent frame. In particular, in both cases, the atomic smashing frame cIdem f ​ ( 𝒱 ) \mathrm{cIdem}_{f}(\mathcal{V}) is spatial. As a first application of our framework, we give a precise meaning to, and compute, the Balmer spectrum for several big t ​ t tt -categories which are not compactly-rigidly generated. The point is that the usual definition of the Balmer spectrum does not directly apply in this generality. Recall that a frame is spatial if it can be realized as the lattice of open subsets of some topological space. Had the telescope conjecture for Sp \mathrm{Sp} held, the spatiality of Idem ⁡ ( Sp ) \mathrm{Idem}(\mathrm{Sp}) would have been immediate, as the Balmer frame Idem f ​ ( Sp ) \mathrm{Idem}_{f}(\mathrm{Sp}) is spatial. The spatiality of Idem ⁡ ( Sp ) \mathrm{Idem}(\mathrm{Sp}) would guarantee the existence of enough prime elements (“points”) to completely recover the frame. This would allow one to classify all smashing localizations via point-set topological methods (such as Stone duality), effectively salvaging the foundational geometric approach to stable homotopy theory in the post-telescope-conjecture world; see [ 9 , 56 ] for a comprehensive study of smashing frames in the spatial case.
